title: Old frontend to new API: retain the consumed response contract
requiredVisibleLabel: Training rehearsal - synthetic data - not a live Azure result
objective: Keep an already-open frontend v1 unchanged, send three fixed journeys to a new API response fixture, and distinguish an additive compatible contract from a breaking renamed field.
preconditions: A modern browser supporting local HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
The old frontend consumes id, displayName and an integer unreadCount.
A fixed baseline and three synthetic GET /api/profile journeys; no real requests.
No account, credentials, authentication, server, framework or Azure subscription.
actions: Choose compatible or breaking new-API responses and complete, partial or absent observations.
Open the old frontend to lock assumptions, then run the candidate journeys.
Inspect response shapes, old-renderer assertions, measurements, gate and synthetic user impact.
Check a prediction independently from the compatibility gate and user impact.
Start another attempt with retained history or explicitly reset all in-memory state.
assertions: An additive theme field leaves the consumed contract and all three rendered results correct.
Renaming displayName to profile.name fails the old renderer even with HTTP 200.
Unobserved responses remain unknown and are never inferred from the selected fixture.
One observed breaking result fails the gate even when other observations are unknown.
Configuration, lifecycle, immutable state and the eight-attempt history limit are guarded.

iac.decisionStage: After genuine loadable-stub behavioral RED and before behavior implementation.
iac.reason: Resource-free local synthetic lesson. Cloud, IaC, scaffolding, identity registration, deployment and expenditure are neither required nor authorized.

limits: Every request, response, profile, HTTP status, rendered result and trace is synthetic.
This portable model proves no real HTTP transport, routing, authentication, protocol or Azure behavior.
No native/source-parent, production Node24, five-nines or unattended browser lifecycle certification.
History retains at most eight completed results in memory and is erased by explicit reset or page reload.
One frozen S unit only; no extra test, evidence, plumbing or refinement credit.
B-S051 and the original D-S051 native acceptance gates remain separate and unfulfilled.
Only learning/S051 is owned; no shared/root, dependency, framework or unsafe browser configuration changes.
